prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one revised FULL MAP concept for Tequila Kill, a top-down western arena. This is the first iteration after a design interview. EXACTLY FOUR small playable character silhouettes, spread around the map so the viewer can assess space for four combatants.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1: previous Arroyo Seco map, CONTENT AND GENERAL ZONING reference. The producer has explicitly approved changing its geometry. Keep its four recognizable places and approximate relative arrangement, but substantially redesign the roads, edges and supporting town fabric. Do not preserve the boxed perimeter wall or huge empty sand areas.
Image 2: APPROVED ART STYLE and Poncho/Garcia identity reference. Preserve softly shaded chunky pixel-art forms, gentle material gradients inside clear stepped outlines, amber wood, cream plaster, muted blue-gray tiled interiors and burgundy accents.
Image 3: FOUR CHARACTER silhouettes reference. Use one of each of its four columns: Poncho, Garcia, brown cowboy hat with blue scarf, pale broad hat with charcoal crown and ochre clothing. The last two are visual placeholders, not new named canonical characters. Ignore all text and all diagram panels.

APPROVED DESIGN BRIEF:
A believable small western frontier town with a MAIN STREET, a SMALL CENTRAL SQUARE, rear ALLEYS and COURTYARDS forming TWO connected alternative loops. Moderately enlarge the previous map to accommodate additional town blocks and routes, not a vast empty desert. Think a first approximate 25 percent linear expansion for study, not a giant sprawling village. The four main places remain accessible, and a few additional closed houses with porches give context and naturally shape the paths.
Replace the continuous enclosing fortress wall with plausible village edges: closed house backs, short courtyard fences, adobe side walls, low dry rocks and scrub at the outer edges. A road should visually suggest the town continues beyond the north and south ends. No continuous rectangular boundary or arena-box wall. Streets are formed by the buildings and their porches. Do not put the town inside a stone fort.

CAMERA AND OUTPUT:
One complete coherent overhead 2D map, landscape approximately 16:10, entire important playable district visible at once, no cropped primary building or hidden route. Classic top-down Zelda-like orthographic projection: floor and roofs seen overhead, small frontal faces on walls, furniture and porches. Horizontal/vertical streets, NO isometric diamond, no perspective vanishing point, no 3D dollhouse or realistic aerial painting. A game-map composition with crisp softly shaded pixel-art assets, matching image 2. No collage, inset, labels, HUD or border.

TOWN ORGANIZATION:
MAIN STREET runs from top center toward bottom center, widening gently into a modest central square. Wood-fronted and adobe western buildings face the street, with raised wooden boardwalks, steps, corner posts and short porches. The square is an intersection and meeting point, not an enormous empty sand rectangle. Use small groups of grounded props at sensible edges to shape cover and crossings without blocking movement.
LEFT / MID-LEFT: SALOON, largest accessible building, roof removed to show its full familiar blue-gray tiled interior. Warm wooden L-shaped bar, mugs/jug, three small card tables with chairs, burgundy couch and rug. Its main doorway faces the central street. Add a short porch or boardwalk outside. A secondary door leads into a rear alley that runs behind it and reconnects to the street.
RIGHT / MID-RIGHT: GENERAL STORE, smaller accessible open-roof shop, visibly DIFFERENT FROM THE SALOON. Counter with weighing scale, sacks, dry goods, small wooden produce boxes and stocked shelves. No poker table, chips, gaming chairs or second bar. A practical goods-loading corner connects with its back alley.
TOP-RIGHT: FENCED YARD connected to the shop/back route, dirt floor, a simple hitching rail or water trough, a crate and barrel storage corner. No horses, animals or extra people. The yard has two clearly usable openings and is part of the right-hand circulation loop.
BOTTOM-LEFT: REMISE / STORAGE SHED with exposed plank floor, organized tools, crates and barrels. Connected to the left rear alley and the southern street.
ADD THREE SMALL CLOSED DWELLINGS around the outer/top-left and bottom-right town edges. Wood or adobe walls, simple brown plank or muted clay roofs, little porches and modest enclosed yards. These houses remain closed and are not extra open-roof combat rooms. Their presence defines believable blocks, intersections, front and back sides. No church, bank, station or extra named landmark.
TWO LOOPS must be visibly continuous: one goes via the saloon side/rear and shed back to the main street, the other via shop side/rear and yard back to the street. Leave generous passable gaps between buildings. No long dead-end one-person corridors, no enormous uninterpreted empty corners. Clear hierarchy: main street, square, smaller side streets, rear courtyards.
Put props in functionally sensible places: freight crates beside loading areas, barrel storage against shed/shop walls, pots beside entrances, modest cart beside a rear service route. Avoid random isolated crates scattered evenly across sand. Use a few cactus/scrub accents at dry outer edges. Exactly one small GREEN TEQUILA BOTTLE rests on the ground in the central square as a visual objective, no ring or glow and no duplicate green decorative bottles.

EXACTLY FOUR READABLE PEOPLE, ONE OF EACH, spread across distinct routes:
1 PONCHO near the saloon's main opening, straw-gold very broad sombrero with raised olive crown, brown cloth hanging VERTICALLY to a broad fringed hem AT FLOOR LEVEL, feet covered. Tight attached shadow, no floating or pointed kite cloth.
2 GARCIA across the central square, broad charcoal hat with small gold star, blue-violet shoulders and red neckerchief, dark trousers and planted boots.
3 BROWN-HAT / BLUE-SCARF placeholder on the upper-right side route between shop and yard. Brown cowboy hat with a distinctive raised brim, blue scarf, dark earthy clothing.
4 PALE-HAT / OCHRE placeholder on the lower route near the shed and southern square. Wide pale straw hat, low charcoal crown and ochre poncho.
All four have similar body scale relative to doors and furniture. Approximately 4 to 5 percent of the entire map height each, legible as game sprites, not portraits. They occupy different areas but are not lost in the far corners. Small held weapons, neutral grounded stances, no shooting, no floating. No NPCs or people in windows, no duplicate characters. Each character's colors distinguish them without UI markers.

ART STYLE:
Faithful to image 2, with gently shaded wood, pots, plaster and cloth, crisp stepped silhouettes and clear square color clusters. Warm golden sand contrasts against quiet cool blue-gray indoor tiles. Low-contrast sparse ground detail and subtle wheel-worn road/footpath variation can describe usage, but no busy grass or stone texture. Timber porches, cream adobe, terracotta pots, amber wood, green cactus accents. All four figures firmly grounded with attached compact contact shadows and consistent upper-left lighting. Keep environment in the same softly shaded pixel-art family as the room reference. No blurry resampling, hyperdetailed painted textures, harsh black floor grid or flat vector poster look.

No text of any kind, no fake signs or written labels, no legend, arrows, route lines, J1/J2/J3/J4, circles, diamonds, HUD, health bars or aiming reticles. No black margins, logo or watermark. This is a new visual-design study, not an implemented engine screenshot or final balance validation.
intent: first progressive village redesign; four figures for scale; artistic mockup only

producer_decisions.problems: Village peu crédible, vide et incohérence ; agrandir et enrichir en gardant la structure générale.
producer_decisions.expansion: Progressive, avec quatre personnages pour apprécier l'espace.
producer_decisions.street_structure: Rue principale, place centrale et parcours de contournement, comme les villes de western.
